title: From Fandom to Checkout: Artificial Intelligence and Immersive Commerce in Professional Sport
content: Professional sport clubs are experimenting with three-dimensional stores, augmented reality, conversational assistants, personalization, gamification, and digitally co-present fan communities. Yet the evidence informing these investments remains dispersed across electronic commerce, immersive technology, artificial intelligence (AI), consumer psychology, and sport management. This integrative review organizes that literature around a central question: how do immersive and AI-enabled interfaces convert fandom into commercially and relationally valuable behavior without weakening trust? The review separates technological features from the experiences and relationships through which they operate and distinguishes peer-reviewed evidence from illustrative club practice. It introduces the Immersive Sport Commerce Conversion Framework (ISCCF), which links five affordance families to fan-experience mechanisms, relational mechanisms, and an outcome ladder extending from exploration to loyalty and responsible data exchange. Team identification, technology readiness, accessibility, culture, and event timing operate as boundary conditions, while privacy, transparency, autonomy, bias, and protection of minors function as governance filters. Eight propositions specify complementarity, mediation, moderation, and backfire effects. The review shows that the strategic opportunity is not a visually richer online shop alone, but an identity-relevant, socially credible, and governable commerce journey. A research agenda prioritizes field experiments, behavioral outcomes, longitudinal designs, cross-market comparisons, and governance-by-design.
